source.title: Second-Order Neural ODE Optimizer
source.authors: Guan-Horng Liu; T. Chen; Evangelos A. Theodorou

record.tranche_reason: The paper compares optimizers and batch sizes using test performance, but does not measure train-test gaps, memorization of random labels, or the specific generalization properties central to most listed versions.
record.gate_note: Test-time results for Adam, SGD, SNOpt, and larger batches are recorded where they bear on V4 or V5. The paper's training-loss curves report convergence over wall-clock time, not a training-versus-test gap. Results cited from other papers are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study compares Adam and momentum SGD on held-out image-classification accuracy in Neural ODEs, bearing on V4 in a new architecture setting. Its batch-size comparisons do not establish the fixed-epoch condition required by V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors emphasize faster wall-clock convergence, competitive test performance, constant memory complexity in integration depth, and further runtime savings from optimizing integration time. Table 17 retains SNOpt's leading image accuracy at batch 512. They do not establish a fixed-epoch large-batch generalization result.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains Neural ODE models with Adam, momentum SGD, and its proposed second-order SNOpt method; it does not use the original studies' memorization or generalization-gap protocols. Learning rate and weight decay are grid-searched per method and dataset.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset changes the Adam-versus-SGD test-accuracy ordering. Batch-size comparison reports results at 128 and 512. The optimizer comparison uses best-tuned results from a learning-rate and weight-decay grid.

fits_no_version.finding: Batch 512 has higher reported mean accuracy than batch 128 for Adam and SGD on all three image datasets, but matched epoch budgets are unspecified.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing batch size from 128 to 512 can preserve or improve Neural ODE image-classification accuracy under the reported training procedure.

record.peer_reviewed: 35th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2021)
record.problems: The study reports test accuracy, not train-test gaps. Its batch-size discussion does not state a fixed epoch budget or provide an explicit matched training-duration comparison. The Adam-versus-SGD results are best-tuned per method and dataset, and the optimizer ordering is mixed across image datasets.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible results omitted. Training-loss convergence curves and test-time performance for time-series and continuous-normalizing-flow tasks do not directly measure the image-classification or language generalization comparisons specified in V4 or V5.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under matched architectures and recipes.
Width sweeps beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.

Learning-rate/schedule-only tuning: weight decay was also searched here. Language benchmarks, matched training performance, optimizer switching, decoupled weight decay, and a controlled comparison of narrow versus broader tuning were not tested.
Matched fixed-epoch batch-size comparisons, workload-dependent thresholds, and controlled tests of compensating recipes. Epoch budgets are not supplied for the batch-128 versus batch-512 results.
Dropout interventions and their dependence on dataset size, dropout strength, or augmentation.
Magnitude-aware weight sharpness, generalization gaps, and ranking against alternative measures.
Removing memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

missing.what: Adam-versus-SGD image accuracy with implicit-adams integration: MNIST 98.86 versus 98.71; SVHN 91.76 versus 94.19; CIFAR10 77.22 versus 76.48.
Matched MALI optimizer comparisons: SVHN Adam+MALI 91.98 versus SGD+MALI 94.33; CIFAR10 77.70 versus 76.41.

record.verdict_notes: A train-test gap is unnecessary to test V4's held-out-performance comparison. Weight-decay tuning prevents treating these results as an exact reproduction of the limited-tuning protocol. R7–R12 are relinked to within-batch optimizer comparisons; their original batch-size contrasts remain descriptive only. Comparator rows duplicate comparisons and should not be counted as independent evidence.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label test performance under the same recipes.
Width sweeps and test error beyond the interpolation threshold.
Comparison of convolutional and fully connected image classifiers or learned local connections.
Language benchmarks, equal-training-performance comparisons, and broader tuning beyond the reported learning-rate and weight-decay grids.
Fixed-epoch comparisons, language models, and workload-dependent batch-size thresholds; the paper reports accuracy at batch sizes 128 and 512.
Dropout comparisons, dropout levels, and interactions with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with train-test gaps.
Removal of memorized training examples and its effect on test accuracy.
